question.text: A manager evaluates setting up a Cat I/II fund in the IFSC at GIFT-City. Which tax benefit is CORRECTLY stated for a GIFT-based AIF under the ITA framework the workbook references?

answer.text: GIFT-City AIFs are EXEMPT from all Indian tax indefinitely

A fund regulated under the IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022 is expressly included in the Section 115UB definition of 'Investment Fund' (FA 2023 amendment) — so pass-through applies just like an onshore SEBI Cat I/II AIF
GIFT AIFs pay a mandatory 10% MAT under Section 115JB
GIFT units attract a 20% STT at redemption

explanation.text: The Logic: Finance Act 2023 amended Section 115UB to expressly include funds regulated under the IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2022. So a GIFT-based Cat I/II AIF gets the same Section 115UB pass-through. Separately, IFSC units enjoy tax holidays under Section 80LA, GST concessions, and specific exemptions on certain transactions — but 'exempt from all Indian tax' is wrong. The key conceptual point here is the 115UB perimeter. The Trap: Option A overstates exemption. Option C fabricates a GIFT-MAT. Option D is not a real rule. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A covers GIFT at a marketing level; XIX-C expects manager-level structural choice-making between onshore and GIFT. Manager's Pro-Tip: Model the structure end-to-end: GIFT onshore manager + IFSC fund + offshore feeders can yield superior net returns for NR LPs. But GIFT's benefits come with strict substance requirements — minimum employee presence, physical office, board composition.
